variants.title: Newton's law of cooling: hot water in a winter laboratory (15 °C)
variants.method: Cooling curve, ln(T - Ts) against t
variants.note: Same vessel as the base lab; only the room is colder, so the excess temperature starts at 75 °C. k does not depend on Ts.

source.title: NCERT Physics Part 2, Class XI, Ch. 10 (Newton's law of cooling)
source.note: Condition: room at 15 °C, a typical North Indian winter laboratory.

variants.title: Newton's law of cooling: hot water in a summer laboratory (35 °C)
variants.method: Cooling curve, ln(T - Ts) against t
variants.note: Same vessel; the room is hot, so the water starts only 55 °C above it and the curve flattens sooner.

source.title: NCERT Physics Part 2, Class XI, Ch. 10 (Newton's law of cooling)
source.note: Condition: room at 35 °C, a typical Indian summer laboratory without air conditioning.

variants.title: Newton's law of cooling: water starting at 70 °C
variants.method: Cooling curve, ln(T - Ts) against t
variants.note: A smaller excess temperature (40 °C) keeps the experiment inside the range where Newton's law holds well; the readings are closer together.

source.title: NCERT Physics Part 2, Class XI, Ch. 10: the law holds for small temperature differences

variants.title: Newton's law of cooling: hot glycerine in the same calorimeter
variants.sample: Glycerine (glycerol), same volume as the water
variants.method: Method of cooling: same vessel, same volume, same surface
variants.unknown: the cooling constant k of glycerine
variants.note: With the same vessel, volume and surface, k is inversely proportional to the heat capacity per volume rho*c. Water: 998 kg/m3 x 4182 J/(kg K); glycerol: 1261 kg/m3 x 2377 J/(kg K), so k(glycerine) = 0.02 x 1.393 = 0.0279 1/s.

source.title: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics: glycerol density 1.261 g/cm3, Cp 218.9 J/(mol K) at 25 °C; water 0.998 g/cm3, 4.182 J/(g K)

variants.title: Newton's law of cooling: hot olive oil in the same calorimeter
variants.sample: Olive oil, same volume as the water
variants.method: Method of cooling: same vessel, same volume, same surface
variants.unknown: the cooling constant k of olive oil
variants.note: Olive oil stores far less heat per volume than water (915 kg/m3 x 1970 J/(kg K) against 998 x 4182), so it cools about 2.3 times faster in the same vessel: k = 0.02 x 2.315 = 0.0463 1/s.

source.title: Engineering ToolBox, Liquids - specific heats (olive oil 1.97 kJ/(kg K)) and densities (olive oil 0.915 g/cm3 at 20 °C)
